clue.text: Study opening for dedicated women

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart
a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: A course of study begins that is meant for women devoted to a calling.
explanation.definitionFit: A convent can mean the community of nuns itself, women devoted to religious life.

clue.text: "The ____ owl, that nightly hoots." (M N Dream)

definitions.text: "The ____ owl, that nightly hoots." (M N Dream)

parts.words: "The ____ owl, that nightly hoots." (M N Dream)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Titania's lullaby scene in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.walkthrough: Titania asks her fairies to keep back the noisy owl in Act 2 Scene 2 of A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing adjective describes a loud, noisy owl in the Shakespeare line quoted.

clue.text: Managed to turn up, estimate, and present an account

indicators.note: in a down clue, to turn up means the word for managed is written bottom to top

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
to rate is to estimate or assess

explanation.surface: A manager arrives, makes a valuation and gives a report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn up' makes RAN read NAR before RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to tell a story, giving an account of events.

clue.text: "The Holly and the Ivy" for example (not Browning)

definitions.text: "The Holly and the Ivy" for example (not Browning)

parts.words: "The Holly and the Ivy" for example (not Browning)
parts.note: the title looks like a poem by Robert Browning, but means plants that never turn brown, and a carol perennially popular

explanation.definitionFit: Holly and ivy keep their leaves all year; the carol is also a perennial favourite, never fading.

clue.text: Mark's muscular spasm and quick end

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitch of a muscle

indicators.note: end of the word quick means its last letter

explanation.surface: Mark suffers a twitch and a sudden death.
explanation.definitionFit: A tick is a small check symbol made against an item on a list.

clue.text: Landed with real trouble, that's true

parts.note: lit is the past tense of light, to land or settle, as a bird lights on a branch

indicators.note: trouble suggests the word real is disturbed and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone arrived bringing genuine difficulties, and that is no lie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges REAL into ERAL, which follows LIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal means exact and factual, so true to the word in the strictest sense.

clue.text: Satirists left men poor as could be

indicators.note: could be hints that the words men poor as might form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Satirical writers left their staff as impoverished as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges MEN POOR AS into AMPOONERS after L.
explanation.definitionFit: Lampoons are mocking satires, so people who write them ridicule their targets.

clue.text: The big-hearted persons pointed out

indicators.note: hearted means the word for big is placed at the centre of the word The

parts.note: OS, outsize, is the clothing abbreviation for big

explanation.surface: Generous folk are being singled out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big-hearted' looks like 'generous'; split it: 'big' is OS, '-hearted' puts it in the heart of THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A demonstrative pronoun for people indicated, as in 'those over there'.

clue.text: Intend to appear in torn clothing

indicators.note: to appear in means the word for intend shows up inside the word for torn

parts.note: rent is a past tense of rend, to tear, so torn
to aim is to intend

explanation.surface: Someone plans to turn up in ripped clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is a literary word for garments or dress.

clue.text: Frivolous, but may be turned on

explanation.surface: Silly, yet capable of being aroused.
explanation.definitionFit: Light entertainment is not serious; a lamp is switched on.

clue.text: About in time for match

indicators.note: in tells us the word for about sits inside the word for time

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
re is Latin-derived shorthand for about or concerning

explanation.surface: Turning up on schedule for a sporting fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: To match is to correspond or be in accord, as two accounts that tally.

clue.text: Making music can be so calming

explanation.surface: Writing a piece of music turns out to be very soothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer is busy writing music; composing oneself also means settling or quieting down.

clue.text: Colourful name of a reigning dynasty

explanation.surface: The vivid title of a royal house that once ruled.
explanation.definitionFit: Orange is a hue; the House of Orange is the royal line of the Netherlands, and William of Orange took the English throne.

clue.text: To stick to no trumps is consistent

parts.note: to cohere is to stick together
NT is the bridge abbreviation for no trumps

explanation.surface: Playing every bridge hand in no trumps shows a steady approach.
explanation.definitionFit: A coherent argument holds together logically, without contradiction.

clue.text: The company readily accepts small change and that serves

parts.note: the table can mean the people seated at it, as in 'the whole table laughed'

indicators.note: accepts means the word for readily takes the small change inside it

parts.note: soon has an old sense of readily, as in 'I would as soon go'
P, a penny, is small change in British money

explanation.surface: The firm happily takes coins, and that does the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' puts P inside SOON to give SPOON after TABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablespoon is the large spoon used for serving food at table.

clue.text: Flora's neat look

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: A woman called Flora has a tidy appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: Flora looks like a woman's name, but it means plant life; 's stands for 'is'. Neat for cattle survives in neatsfoot oil.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxeye daisy is a common wild flower, an example of plant life.

clue.text: Seaman observed coming back carrying weapon rejects

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: carrying means one word holds another inside it
coming back means the word for observed is read backwards

parts.note: seen means observed
gat is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A sailor, spotted returning with a gun, turns things down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns SEEN into NEES, and 'carrying' puts GAT inside it to give NEGATES after AB.
explanation.definitionFit: To abnegate is to renounce or deny oneself something, so to refuse it.

clue.text: Old fighter gleeful about a riot breaking out

parts.note: glad means pleased or gleeful

indicators.note: breaking out suggests the words a riot break apart and regroup

explanation.surface: An ancient warrior is delighted about violence erupting in the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link; 'breaking out' rearranges A RIOT into IATOR after GLAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladiators fought in Roman arenas, combatants from antiquity.

clue.text: The dope the prime minister is upset to reveal

indicators.note: is upset says the letters for the prime minister plus is are knocked into a new order

parts.note: PM is the abbreviation for prime minister
to let on is to reveal a secret

explanation.surface: The fool leading the government is unhappy at being exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges PM and IS into SIMP, followed by LET ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is a stupid person, a fool or idiot.

clue.text: Foreigner admitting money could make him an assassin

indicators.note: admitting means letting the money in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a stranger is an outsider or foreigner
L stands for pound, from Latin libra, a unit of money

explanation.surface: An outsider who takes a bribe might turn into a hired killer.
explanation.definitionFit: A strangler kills by throttling, a murderer of a particular kind.

clue.text: Decide to separate

explanation.surface: Make up one's mind to split up.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a firm decision; also, in chemistry or optics, to break into component parts.

clue.text: A trainee member's fear

parts.note: L is the learner plate on a British trainee driver's car
an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A new recruit to a club is nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is sudden fright or anxiety at danger.

clue.text: Trade is bad, though up

indicators.note: bad indicates the words Trade is are in poor shape and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Business is poor even though prices have risen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' here means mounted, as on a horse; the economic surface suggests rising figures.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider who is up sits with a leg on each side of the horse.

clue.text: The underworld boss writes note authorising share out

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld
to pen is to write
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A gangland chief puts his signature to a memo approving a payout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'authorising' is a link; the mafia picture of 'underworld boss' hides the classical god Dis.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispense is to distribute or hand round in portions.

clue.text: Put off some people with crude terminology

indicators.note: some means only part of the words crude terminology is taken

explanation.surface: Coarse language deters certain listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter is to discourage someone from doing something.

clue.text: Follow leaderless men, and start action

indicators.note: leaderless means the word men loses its first letter

parts.note: to sue is to start legal action

explanation.surface: Men without a commander go after the enemy and launch an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come after as a result.

clue.text: A braggart may well get fired

explanation.surface: A boastful employee is likely to lose his job.
explanation.walkthrough: Pistol is the swaggering braggart in Shakespeare's Henry IV and Henry V.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's boastful soldier bears this name; a handgun is something discharged by a shot.

clue.text: They're available in many shades hundreds certainty

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, a number of hundreds
yes expresses assent with certainty

explanation.surface: Colours for sale in a wide range, and plenty of them for sure.
explanation.definitionFit: Colouring agents come in a vast range of tints.

clue.text: A highly romantic tale

parts.note: read literally, a narrative that is lofty in height; in fact a fanciful, hard-to-believe yarn

explanation.definitionFit: A tale exaggerated past belief, highly fanciful rather than romantic in the love sense.

clue.text: Oliver the screw

explanation.surface: Oliver plays the villain of the piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver is Dickens's orphan hero of that surname; to screw a cap on is to turn it round.

clue.text: A school for girls — awfully dear one!

indicators.note: awfully suggests the words dear one are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A girls' school, an exclaimed comment on what an expensive one costs.
explanation.walkthrough: ROEDEAN is a famous fee-paying girls' boarding school near Brighton, England.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-known English independent boarding school for girls.

clue.text: Take issue about press operator

indicators.note: about means one word goes round the other

parts.note: issue means offspring, so a son
to press someone is to urge them

explanation.surface: Disagreeing with what the newspapers say about a machine worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' is a link. 'issue' reads as a dispute but means children; 'operator' is not a machinist but one who operates.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon performs operations, so is one who operates on patients.
